The assumed additional use of 5.26 million pounds of plastics could result in a minor increase in the solid waste disposal problem. Plastics not recycled will present a problem if they are disposed of by deposit in sanitary landfills. When deposited in sanitary landfills, plastics and other light objects tend to rise over a period of time. Plastics, in particular, do not readily decompose. Thus, infusion of a substantial quantity of plastics will tend to put off the time when the landfill can be put to other uses. Moreover, deposit of almost any materials will fill up a landfill sooner, requiring greater use of land for sanitary landfills.

IRREVERSIBLE AND IRRETRIEVABLE COMMITMENT OF RESOURCES
An area of impact on natural resources is an increase in the use and size of catalytic converters and the resultant increase in demand for platinum and palladium. This increase in size will increase total platinum and palladium use by 2.7 percent for NPA's of 6,000 pounds GVWR and less. This would increase the EPA's estimate of 180,000 troy ounces for all NPA's of 10,000 pounds and less GVWR by an additional 2,200 troy ounces to 182,200 troy ounces.
